_comment: Models benchmarked by scripts/model_benchmark.py. 'selected' ones become the AppConfig model catalog. All passed a live Converse tool-use probe in this account on 2026-10-14 (MiniMax M2.5 and DeepSeek V3.2 added the same day; DeepSeek R1 rejected: no tool use in Converse). Claude 5.x models are omitted: the account's applied Bedrock quota for them is 0.

candidates.name: Claude Opus 4.6
candidates.strengths: Deepest reasoning and most careful tool use; best at subtle cases (fraud signals, coverage disputes).
candidates.tradeoffs: Highest price per token and among the slowest candidates.

candidates.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
candidates.strengths: Near-Opus quality on agentic tool use at about 60% of the price; the app's original model.
candidates.tradeoffs: Adaptive thinking makes each analysis take a minute or more.

candidates.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
candidates.strengths: Fast, inexpensive Claude that still follows long tool schemas well.
candidates.tradeoffs: Run without extended thinking here, so it can miss multi-signal judgment calls.

candidates.name: Amazon Nova Pro
candidates.strengths: AWS first-party multimodal model; low price with solid tool use.
candidates.tradeoffs: Less precise than Claude on long structured outputs.

candidates.name: Amazon Nova 2 Lite
candidates.strengths: AWS first-party, very low cost and fast; large context window.
candidates.tradeoffs: Smaller model: weaker on nuanced judgment.

candidates.name: Llama 4 Maverick 17B
candidates.strengths: Meta's open-weight mixture-of-experts model (17B active of 400B); very cheap and the fastest per call.
candidates.tradeoffs: Less reliable with large nested tool schemas and long structured outputs.

candidates.name: OpenAI gpt-oss-120b
candidates.strengths: Open-weight reasoning model; the lowest price per token and very low latency.
candidates.tradeoffs: In-region only (no cross-region profile); open-weight models trail Claude on grounding discipline.

candidates.name: MiniMax M2.5
candidates.strengths: Open-weight agentic/coding model with built-in interleaved reasoning; strong multi-step tool use at a very low price.
candidates.tradeoffs: In-region only (no cross-region profile); always reasons, so output tokens and latency run higher than other low-cost models.

candidates.name: DeepSeek V3.2
candidates.strengths: Open-weight frontier-class MoE model with sparse attention; strong general reasoning at a low price.
candidates.tradeoffs: In-region only; needs firm instructions to call tools (sometimes leaks its tool-call markup into text).
